queries.hook: A fire lit by seeing what others achieved; the resolve to rise, gather your strength and take on what is yours to do.
queries.diagnose: Resolve fades when the mind runs ahead to the prize or looks sideways at others; it holds when the work itself is the reward.
queries.steady: No honest effort on the right path is ever wasted; even a little of it protects you and carries you forward.
queries.act: Rise and act; do your work fully and well each day, let the result go, and keep at it when no one is watching.
queries.story: A story of someone who set out to build or win something that was theirs to do, met the first test, and kept going.

hook.speaker: Vibhishan
hook.setting: Vibhishan, standing before Ram, names who he is and asks for shelter.
hook.sanskrit: श्रवन सुजसु सुनि आयउँ प्रभु भंजन भव भीर। त्राहि त्राहि आरति हरन सरन सुखद रघुबीर ॥
hook.line: I heard of you and came. Save me, you who take away distress.
hook.translation: Hearing your good name with my own ears I have come, Lord, breaker of the fear of the world. Save me, save me, remover of distress, Raghubir, whose refuge brings joy.
hook.why: The turning itself is enough to be taken in; your past is not the deciding question.

prasang.title: Vibhishan crosses over: Ram's refuge speech
prasang.summary: Kicked out of Lanka for telling his brother the truth, Vibhishan crosses the sea to Ram, dreaming of his feet. Sugriva wants him bound as a spy; Ram says his vow is to remove the fear of anyone who comes for refuge, and if the visitor were truly wicked he would not have come at all. Ram embraces him, asks how he kept his goodness among the cruel, describes the devotee who ties every thread of love to him, and crowns him king, shyly giving what Ravana got for ten heads.
prasang.story_hook: Kicked out by his own brother, a man stood on the far shore and wondered whether the enemy he was walking toward would let him in.
prasang.lesson: The turning itself is enough to be taken in; your past is not the deciding question.

verse.speaker: Tulsidas
verse.setting: Tulsidas asks Hanuman to forgive what he said in distress.
verse.sanskrit: अति आरत, अति स्वारथी, अति दीन-दुखारी। इनको बिलगु न मानिये, बोलहिं न बिचारी॥ … नाकहि आये नाथसों, साँसति भय भारी। कहि आयो, कीबी छमा, निज ओर निहारी॥
verse.line: Don't hold it against the hurting; they speak without thinking. Forgive me, looking from your side.
verse.translation: The very distressed, the very needy, the very poor and hurting: do not take offence at them; they speak without thinking. I had reached my limit, Lord; the suffering and fear were heavy. I said what I said; forgive me, looking at it from your side.
verse.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.

plan_v3.writer_note: Letting-go teaching for a reader who is building something. Explain it through their own situation and feeling: what is released is the grip that hurts them, never their love, their hope or their work. Never say or imply 'stop caring' or 'your hope is the problem'. Read it after the guard verse, which reassures first.

guard.line: Turn to me with your whole heart, and I will carry what you lack and guard what you have.

verse.speaker: Hanuman
verse.setting: Hanuman, having given Ram's message, comforts Sita.
verse.sanskrit: कह कपि हृदयँ धीर धरु माता। सुमिरु राम सेवक सुखदाता॥ उर आनहु रघुपति प्रभुताई। सुनि मम बचन तजहु कदराई ॥
verse.line: Hold steady, mother. Remember Ram, and let my words take away your fear.
verse.translation: Hanuman said: 'Hold steady in your heart, mother. Remember Ram, who gives joy to his servants. Bring to mind Raghupati's strength; hearing my words, put away your fear.'
verse.for_you: The path you want to walk is opening. Let the memory of what steadies you fill your heart today.
verse.try_today: Recall the strength that holds the world steady.
verse.scene_line: You sit with Hanuman, holding steady as you remember Ram.

why: fear is answered by recalling whose strength stands behind her

verse.speaker: Vidura
verse.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verse.sanskrit: न देवा यष्टिमादाय रक्षन्ति पशुपालवत् / यं तु रक्षितुमिच्छन्ति बुद्ध्या संयोजयन्ति तम्
verse.line: The gods don't stand guard with a stick; whom they protect, they give clear judgement.
verse.translation: The gods do not guard a person with a stick in hand, the way a herdsman guards cattle. Whomever they wish to protect, they endow with good judgement.
verse.why: Character shows under pressure. Do by day what will let you sleep at night.

prasang.title: Vidura Niti: Keshini's choice and the tests of character
prasang.summary: Vidura tells how Prahlada judged honestly against his own son when Princess Keshini set two suitors a test, then gives aphorisms: gold is tested by fire, friends by hard times, and a clear conscience lets you sleep.
prasang.lesson: Character shows under pressure. Do by day what will let you sleep at night.

verse.for_you: The gods do not guard you with a stick. They give sound judgement to whom they protect. Let this be your shelter today.
verse.try_today: Notice the moment today when your thinking feels clearest and let it guide your next step.

why: Protection is located in clear thinking

verse.speaker: Seer
verse.sanskrit: अग्ने नय सुपथा राये अस्मान् विश्वानि देव वयुनानि विद्वान् । युयोध्यस्मज्जुहुराणमेनो भूयिष्ठां ते नमौक्तिं विधेम ॥
verse.line: Lead us by the good path. Keep crooked dealing far from us.
verse.translation: O Agni, lead us by the good path to true wealth, O god who knows all our ways. Keep crooked wrongdoing away from us. We offer you our fullest words of reverence.
verse.why: Hold what you have lightly, keep working, and see yourself in everyone.

prasang.title: The Isha: enjoy by letting go
prasang.summary: Eighteen verses that open by saying everything belongs to the divine, so we should enjoy it without grasping. They go on to say we should work a full life without being bound, and see ourselves in all beings.
prasang.lesson: Hold what you have lightly, keep working, and see yourself in everyone.

why: trust that there is a good path
the one who knows all our ways is asked to lead

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna's final counsel: act with devotion, reflect, choose, and take refuge.
verse.sanskrit: इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं मया । विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥
verse.line: I've told you all I know. Reflect on it fully, then do as you choose.
verse.translation: Thus I have declared to you this knowledge, more secret than all secrets. Reflect on it fully, and then do as you wish.
verse.why: Reflect fully, choose freely, and set down the fear.

prasang.title: Action with devotion: surrender
prasang.summary: Krishna urges Arjuna to offer all action, warns that ego will only trip him, tells him to reflect fully and then choose, and finally to take refuge in him alone and not grieve.
prasang.lesson: Reflect fully, choose freely, and set down the fear.

verse.for_you: The path ahead is yours to choose after you have thought it through. Your own resolve will guide you once you have looked at it clearly.
verse.try_today: Notice one choice you make today and hold it as your own.

why: Reflect fully, then decide and begin.
the choice made after reflection is one's own

story.title: Uddalaka's lessons: tat tvam asi
story.summary: Uddalaka teaches his son through everyday experiments: a fast that dims the mind, a bird on a string, rivers merging in the sea, a banyan seed with nothing visible inside, salt dissolved in water, a blindfolded man finding his way home. Each lesson ends: 'That subtle essence is the self of all. You are that, Shvetaketu.'
story.lesson: What is most real in you is unseen, everywhere, and the same in all.
story.for_you: The path to Vrindavan is not the same as a dead end. Someone can point you toward it, and your own steps will take you there.
